claims.statement: backupFile never destroys a recoverable file: it skips the write when the target already equals what is about to be written, and never replaces a .bak DocGuard did not write.

faults.description: [line 26] Guard removed: `if (nextContent !== null && content === nextContent) return;` no longer runs.
[line 36] Guard never triggers: `if (prior !== content)` becomes `if (false)`.

claims.statement: A persisted benchmark baseline is quotable only when its metrics and caveat are recomputable from its retained cases: the loader rejects a hand-edited ratio, a stale caveat, a measure other than benchmark-precision, and the pre-provenance envelope, before any benchmark run starts.

faults.description: Metrics integrity check removed: a hand-edited core.metrics is accepted.
Caveat check removed: a stale or edited review.caveat is accepted.
Measure check removed: review.measures may claim calibration.
Legacy envelope guard removed: a schemaVersion 1 baseline without provenance is no longer refused with the regeneration message.

claims.statement: A finding code the reviewed corpus never exercised reports that it is unmeasured and quotes no rate: it never inherits the measured precision of other codes in its validator, and a measured code below the published floor never has its point estimate quoted on its own.

faults.description: Unmeasured codes fall through to their validator cell, inventing evidence for 97 of 104 codes.
The minN floor is removed: a rate from a single labelled finding becomes quotable.
Backoff is offered to every code, not only measured ones below the floor.
False positives are attributed to every code in a case scope instead of the code named by the finding identity.

claims.statement: docguard init invokes specify with an explicit, non-interactive --integration and never with the options Spec Kit 0.10 removed; a failed delegation is reported as failed, never as initialized.

faults.description: Initialization reverts to the removed --ai option.
A failed specify init is reported as initialized.
faults.find: return { status: 'failed', integration, reason: failureReason(err), manualCommand, extension: notAttempted };
faults.replace: return { status: 'initialized', integration, reason: null, manualCommand: null, extension: notAttempted };

claims.statement: specs require never passes a governed change on a reference to a spec that does not exist, and an inconclusive run exits non-zero.

faults.description: An unresolved specs/<dir> reference counts as covered.
Inconclusive exits 0.
faults.find: const SPEC_FIRST_EXIT = { covered: 0, exempt: 0, 'not-governed': 0, uncovered: 1, inconclusive: 2 };
faults.replace: const SPEC_FIRST_EXIT = { covered: 0, exempt: 0, 'not-governed': 0, uncovered: 1, inconclusive: 0 };

claims.statement: Guard coverage counts Spec Kit feature artifacts and the constitution in the specKit tier, never as untiered.

faults.description: The Spec Kit tier is never assigned.

claims.statement: A documented runtime-dependency count that package.json contradicts produces MET004.

faults.description: Every dependency claim passes.

claims.statement: An AGENTS.md chain larger than its budget or allowance produces STR004.

faults.description: No chain is ever over budget.

claims.statement: Every consumer of .docguardignore honours gitignore-style dir/ patterns through the single shared parser.

faults.description: loadIgnorePatterns ignores nothing.

claims.statement: Bare TODO/FIXME count only as the first word of a comment; ordinary words and keyword lists never become annotations.

faults.description: Bare TODO/FIXME recognition is dropped.
The bare form matches anywhere in the comment.

claims.statement: docguard hooks never writes into a husky, lefthook or simple-git-hooks hooks directory, even with --force.

faults.description: Hook-manager detection is bypassed.

claims.statement: A spec with checked tasks and no @implements evidence produces SPR006.

faults.description: Specs with checked tasks are always treated as annotated.
Unmerged paths are counted once per stage again.

claims.statement: With unreadable git metadata, history-based validators report missing-prerequisite instead of no-matches.

faults.description: Freshness treats unreadable metadata as no repository.
Diff-Suspicion treats unreadable metadata as no repository.
Reference-Existence treats unreadable metadata as no repository.
The Spec-Kit untouched-task check stays silent on unreadable metadata.
An unreadable .git is classified as no repository at all.

claims.statement: An as-built spec is registered with origin as_built and its source paths, and guard reports both code the spec does not account for and cited facts that no longer exist.

faults.description: Vanished facts are never reported.
Unclaimed facts are never reported.
generate --spec --write does not record origin.
The registry drops origin when it re-serializes.
Env vars read outside the area become candidates for it.
generate --spec falls through to the doc generator.
The CLI never parses --spec.
SPR007 is not a registered finding code.
A failed registry write leaves the spec directory behind.
faults.find: try { rmdirSync(dirname(abs)); } catch { /* the directory is not empty or already gone */ }

claims.statement: SPK010 counts a named directory as touched when the feature changed a path strictly under it, and still reports a directory with nothing changed inside.

faults.description: Directory claims are never matched against nested changes.
A sibling directory sharing the prefix vouches for it.
Any change under a file's directory vouches for the file.

claims.statement: An unattended release cuts the version its curated changelog describes, publishes the reviewed notes, pins the CLI its Action installs, renders Homebrew only from verified registry bytes, and its help and schema name what the code accepts.

faults.description: Added entries no longer make a minor release.
The cut drops the curated notes.
An existing version section is overwritten.
Release sync stops moving the Action's CLI pin.
A tampered tarball is trusted.
faults.find: if (actual !== m[1]) throw new Error('downloaded tarball does not match npm dist.integrity');
faults.replace: if (false) throw new Error('downloaded tarball does not match npm dist.integrity');

faults.description: Release PRs may not change action.yml.
Top-level help drops `specs require`.

claims.statement: reconcile links a change to a requirement declared in a canonical document it cites, and never to an undeclared or escaping citation.

faults.description: Canonical links are never recorded.
Undeclared IDs are linked.
A path escape is followed.
A co-changed canonical document is not treated as intent.

claims.statement: Every finding carries severity, disposition, confidence, evidence and parserTier as independent channels: an explicit valid disposition wins, only the exact string 'low' means low confidence, parserTier accepts only the benchmark vocabulary, and evidence reports measured only for codes the reviewed corpus measures.

faults.description: Explicit disposition ignored: disposition is always derived from the suggestion kind, so disposition 'act' on a finding without a fix suggestion becomes 'escalate'.
Confidence coercion inverted: anything other than the exact string 'high' (null, 'medium', 'review') becomes 'low', labelling certain observations uncertain.
parserTier vocabulary check removed: any value (including undefined, 'ast', 7) passes through instead of defaulting to 'not-applicable'.
isMeasured always true: a never-benchmarked code claims measured status.

claims.statement: Default feedback selection offers every finding whose code is unmeasured or whose confidence is low, and discloses the measured, confident findings it excludes, with --all excluding nothing.

faults.description: reportable no longer includes unmeasured codes: a confident finding on a never-benchmarked code is not sampled, restoring the closed loop.
Default selection ignores reportable: `docguard feedback` offers nothing unless --all or --code is passed.
Excluded set hidden: the default selection reports zero excluded findings even when measured, confident findings were left out.
--all no longer clears the excluded set: an --all run still reports findings as excluded.

claims.statement: A reviewed disagreement is recorded as an auditable corpus row that is counted per code and corpus-wide, enters no precision, recall or abstention denominator, and whose removal fails baseline comparison.

faults.description: Measured-class filter removed: adjudicated rows enter cases, repositories and repair denominators.
policy_disagreement rows no longer counted: the disagreement vanishes from the per-code and corpus-wide adjudicated counts.
Case-removed regression not reported: deleting an adjudication row from the corpus passes baseline comparison.
faults.find: regressions.push({ id, kind: 'case-removed', detail: 'A baseline case is absent from the candidate.' });

faults.description: Opposite-control requirement dropped: buildAdjudicationRow accepts a manifest with no neighbouring clean case.

claims.statement: A documented endpoint missing from the OpenAPI contract is reported as a review-only error with separate low-confidence code evidence (present, not-found or unknown), and neither the validator nor `docguard fix --write`, forced or not, ever deletes it from the API reference.

faults.description: Contract-omission suggestion becomes an actionable fix instead of a review, so a code-present omission is dispositioned 'act'.
Unknown coverage collapsed into not-found: when no routes were extracted, every omission claims the route scan did not find it.
Negative route-scan evidence reported at high confidence, overstating what an incomplete scanner can prove.
applyApiSurfaceWrites reports the not-found omissions as removed, authorizing deletion from negative route-scan evidence.

claims.statement: Password and skipped-test warnings are withheld only on proven context: a password inside an expect(...) mock expectation is exempt only for explicit synthetic vocabulary and downgraded only when the literal repeats, and a skipped test is explained only by a non-empty static reason argument or a directly adjacent REASON comment.

faults.description: Repeat threshold lowered to one occurrence: every password in a test assertion is treated as a repeated fixture and downgraded to a low-confidence warning.
Receiver check removed: any `.toHaveBeenCalledWith(...)` call, not only one on expect(...), exempts a synthetic-looking password.
Whitespace-only skip reason accepted as an explanation.
Adjacency check removed: a REASON comment separated from the skip by intervening code still explains it.

claims.statement: No module in cli/validators/ imports a sibling validator module; shared logic lives in shared modules (Constitution IV).

faults.description: api-surface.mjs gains a working named import of the changelog validator.
faults.replace:
import { mkFinding, resultFromFindings } from '../findings.mjs';
import { validateChangelog } from './changelog.mjs';

faults.description: docs-sync.mjs re-imports the api-surface validator, the historical Constitution IV violation.
faults.replace:
import { findAllOpenApiSpecs } from '../shared-openapi.mjs';
import { validateApiSurface } from './api-surface.mjs';

claims.statement: Several completions can share one revision, a recorded revision off HEAD's history is reported, and re-anchoring moves it only to a commit with byte-identical evidence or an attested revision.

faults.description: Outcome-only spec edits count as changes, so batches block.
Spec prose edits are treated as lifecycle-only.
A revision off HEAD's history is not reported.

faults.replace: else if (false) out.push({ specId: spec.specId, revision, reason: 'not-ancestor' });

faults.description: Re-anchoring accepts a target whose evidence differs.

faults.description: An unresolvable revision is re-anchored without an attestation.
The off-default-branch warning is never raised.
Stripping the outcome block leaves it in place, so an outcome-only change blocks the batch.
Re-anchoring does not move the outcome line in the spec.

claims.statement: sync --since narrows exactly the generated sections the plan emits, and a docs-only change refreshes none of them.

faults.description: A section keeps its old table-suffixed ID.
Docs changes count as code.
tech-stack refreshes on any code change.

claims.statement: A PR that makes guard slower past its budget, adds an error finding, grows agent-facing bytes, adds a dependency, or cannot be measured against its base does not pass silently; only a declared Budget-Exempt waives one metric.

faults.description: The floor is ignored, so noise fails.
faults.find: const limit = Math.max(base * maxRatio, base + floor);

faults.description: A breach passes.
faults.find: if (head <= limit) return row(metric, base, head, budget, 'PASS');
faults.replace: if (true) return row(metric, base, head, budget, 'PASS');

faults.description: An unmeasured base passes.
faults.find: if (!Number.isFinite(base)) return row(metric, base, head, null, 'INCONCLUSIVE', 'base could not be measured');
faults.replace: if (!Number.isFinite(base)) return row(metric, base, head, null, 'PASS');

faults.description: A new dependency passes.
An exemption without a reason is accepted.
Interleaving stops: head always runs second.
